## Loading libraries
```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(wordcloud)
library(janeaustenr)
```
## Intro into {stringr}

### What is a string?
A string and a character are the same thing. You can tell something is a string by the presence of quotations.
```{r}
words <- "This is a string"
words

words_vector <- c("Apples", "Bananas", "Oranges")
words_vector
```


### 1. Manipulation:

Paste:
```{r}
paste("High temp", "Low pH") #pasting words together
paste("High temp", "Low pH", sep = "-") #adding dash between words
paste0("High temp", "Low pH") #removing the space in between words
```

Working with vectors:
```{r}
shapes <- c("Square", "Circle", "Triangle")
paste("My favorite shape is a", shapes)
```
```{r}
two_cities <- c("best", "worst")
paste("It was the", two_cities, "of times.")
```

Individual characters:
```{r}
shapes
str_length(shapes) #how long a string is; how many letters are in each word
```
```{r}
seq_data <- c("ATCCCGTC")
str_sub(seq_data, start = 2, end = 4) #extract from the 2nd amino acid to the 4th AA
```

Modifying strings:
```{r}
str_sub(seq_data, start = 3, end = 3) <- "A" #add an A in the 3rd position
seq_data
```
```{r}
str_dup(seq_data, times = c(2, 3)) #times = the number of times to duplicate each string
```


### 2. Whitespace

Have some words with extra white spaces:
```{r}
badtreatments <- c("High", " High", "High ", "Low", "Low")
badtreatments
```
Trimming white space:
```{r}
str_trim(badtreatments) #this removes white space from both sides
```
```{r}
str_trim(badtreatments, side = "left") #this removes from only the left side
```

Adding white space:
```{r}
str_pad(badtreatments, 5, side = "right") #add a white space to the right side after the 5th character (each will be 5 characters for the final)
```
Adding a character instead of white space:
```{r}
str_pad(badtreatments, 5, side = "right", pad = "1") # add a 1 to the right side after the 5th character
```


### 3. Locale sensitive:

Make everything upper case:
```{r}
x <- "I love R!"
str_to_upper(x)
```
Lower case:
```{r}
str_to_lower(x)
```
Title case:
```{r}
str_to_title(x)
```

### 4. Pattern matching:

View a specific pattern in a vector of strings:
```{r}
data <- c("AAA", "TATA", "CTAG", "GCTT")
str_view(data, pattern = "A")
```

Detect a specific pattern:
```{r}
str_detect(data, pattern = "A")
str_detect(data, pattern = "AT")
```

Locate a pattern:
```{r}
str_locate(data, pattern = "AT")
```
## {regex}: Regular Expressions

### Metacharacters:

```{r}
vals <- c("a.b", "b.c", "c.d")
```

replace all the “.” with a space
```{r}
# string, pattern, replace
str_replace(vals, "\\.", " ")
```

Default only replaces first:
```{r}
vals <- c("a.b.c", "b.c.d", "c.d.e")
# string, pattern, replace
str_replace(vals, "\\.", " ")
```
Replacing all:
```{r}
# string, pattern, replace
str_replace_all(vals, "\\.", " ")
```

### Sequences:

Subsetting a vector to keep only string with digits:
```{r}
val2 <- c("test 123", "test 456", "test")

str_subset(val2, "\\d") #finding strings with difits
```

### Character class:

Count the number of lowercase vowels in each string:
```{r}
str_count(val2, "[aeiou]")
```

Count any digit:
```{r}
str_count(val2, "[0-9]")
```


### Quantifiers:

Example: find the phone numbers:
```{r}
strings <- c("550-153-7578",
             "banana",
             "435.114.7586",
             "home: 672-442-6739")
```

Create a regex that finds all strings that contain a phone number
```{r}
phone <- "([2-9][0-9]{2})[- .]([0-9]{3})[- .]([0-9]{4})"
#first # between 2-9, the next two are between 0-9 ({2} means 2 previous), then a dash or a dot, then 3 between 0-9, another dash and dot, and then 4 numbers between 0-9

str_detect(strings, phone)
```
```{r}
# subset only the strings with phone numbers
test <- str_subset(strings, phone)
test
```

Replace all the “.” with “-” and extract only the numbers (leaving the letters behind). Remove any extra white space.
```{r}
test |>
  str_replace_all("\\.", "-") |>
  str_replace_all("[a-zA-Z]", "") |>
  str_replace_all("\\:", "") |>
  str_replace_all(" ", "")
```


## {tidytext}

Using Jane Austen's books:
```{r}
head(austen_books())
tail(austen_books())
glimpse(austen_books())
```
Clean it up and add a column for line and chapter:
```{r}
original_books <- austen_books() |> # get all of Jane Austen's books
  group_by(book) |>
  mutate(line = row_number(), # find every line
         chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text, regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]", # count the chapters (starts with (^) the word chapter followed by any digit or a roman numeral); cumulative sum so they're in order (assumes ch 2 after ch 1 etc)
                                                 ignore_case = TRUE)))) |> # ignore lower or uppercase
  ungroup() # ungroup it so we have a dataframe again

# don't try to view the entire thing... it's >73000 lines...
head(original_books)
```

Text mining: make it only one word per row so it's tidy:
```{r}
tidy_books <- original_books |>
  unnest_tokens(output = word, input = text) # add a column named word, with the input as the text column

head(tidy_books)
glimpse(tidy_books)
```
Stopwords: words that are common and don’t really have important meaning
```{r}
# see an example of all the stopwords
head(get_stopwords())
```
Removing all stopwords:
```{r}
cleaned_books <- tidy_books |>
  anti_join(get_stopwords()) # dataframe without the stopwords

head(cleaned_books)
```
Counting the most common words (excluding stopwords) across all her books:
```{r}
cleaned_books |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE)
```

Sentiment analysis: (positive vs. negative words)
```{r}
sent_word_counts <- tidy_books |>
  inner_join(get_sentiments()) |> # only keep pos or negative words
  count(word, sentiment, sort = TRUE) # count them

head(sent_word_counts)
```
Visualize positive and negative words:
```{r}
sent_word_counts |>
  filter(n > 150) |> # take only if there are over 150 instances of it
  mutate(n = ifelse(sentiment == "negative", -n, n)) |> # add a column where if the word is negative make the count negative
  mutate(word = reorder(word, n)) |> # sort it so it goes from largest to smallest
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = word, fill = sentiment)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(y = "Contribution to sentiment")
```

Making a wordcloud:
```{r}
words <- cleaned_books |>
  count(word) |> # count all the words
  arrange(desc(n)) |> # sort the words
  slice(1:100) # take the top 100

wordcloud(words = words$word, freq = words$n, colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))
#freq = words$n makes words larger based on how many times they appeared
```
